issues.body: Section 5.3 item 4 requires the deny message for an out-of-scope quad and a nonexistent quad to be byte-identical. But L2 and section 5.1 evaluate DELETE against the masked fork: a nonexistent or masked triple creates no delete effect, so the operation succeeds as a no-op and no deny message exists. Section 4 explicitly confirms that masked DELETE reports success. Thus the mandatory test cannot be implemented as written and conflates the insert scope-boundary rule (L3) with delete nonexistence indistinguishability (L2).
issues.fix_hint: Split the acceptance requirement by operation. For INSERT membership probes, assert identical verdict/store/subsequent-read behavior for masked-present and masked-absent cases (as item 3 already does). For DELETE, assert identical successful no-op behavior for masked-present and absent triples. Reserve byte-identical denial checks for two cases that both actually deny under L3/L8, and state exactly which cases those are. Update L7 wording if it currently implies that nonexistent DELETE is denied.
issues.title: L7 acceptance test requires a denial that the proposed semantics never produce

verdict.summary: The design is candid about its non-implemented status, the live graph-granularity WHERE leak, and the unresolved blank-node replay question. The masked-replica/delta/replay construction is otherwise coherent with the parent read-scope record and the existing atomic-denial test. However, the stated L7 acceptance test is internally inconsistent with L2 and the proposed algorithm: a nonexistent or masked DELETE produces no captured delta and succeeds, so there is no denial message to compare with an out-of-scope insertion denial. The acceptance bar must specify comparable operations and observable outcomes before this record can serve as an implementation contract.
